toolchain: Node 24.21.0, Vitest 4.1.11 (vitest bench via the Node API)
runner: developer workstation, 3 runs of the whole suite, each its own fresh node process (docs/PROGRESS.md step 2.11 — an earlier version of this file ran all 3 in one process and that cross-run warm-up was itself the dominant source of spread, not real noise) — not a dedicated CI runner class; numbers are indicative, not tight. Machine conditions: plugged in (not on battery), no other heavy applications open, file parallelism disabled and a single worker (fileParallelism: false — see scripts/bench-guard.mjs), no other vitest process running concurrently (enforced for other bench runs via a PID lock; an unrelated `npm test`/`vitest watch` process is a manual check, documented in PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §9 — cross-platform process-list inspection was judged impractical here).
note: docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §9: 'CI fails when a benchmark regresses > 20% against the baseline on the same runner class.' `npm run bench:compare` (scripts/bench-compare.mjs) checks that threshold against this file (single run, compared to the median below); it is run at gates, not in `npm run check`. Regenerate this file with `npm run bench:baseline` (scripts/generate-baseline.mjs, 3 runs). Each entry's `p99Runs` is that run's own p99, in run order; `p99Ms` is their median, which is what `pass` is computed on; `p99SpreadPct` is `(max - min) / median` across the 3 runs, and an entry over 25% also gets a `noisy` field — nothing is hidden (CLAUDE.md §1.5).
budgetSource: docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §2, design tier (docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §1: 2,000 entities / 5,000 reactions / 15,000 relationships+mappings); stress-tier entries use §1's "budgets may degrade <= 2x" allowance as an informal budget (no §2 row of its own).
verdictBasis: median p99 across 3 runs, as a conservative stand-in for §2's p95 budgets — `vitest bench` (tinybench) reports p75/p99/p995/p999 but not p95, and a single run's p99 is too noisy to judge alone (docs/PROGRESS.md step 2.10 measured the same scenario at 35.6 ms and 92-107/120-129 ms across runs). `pass` below is computed on the median of 3 p99s; a p95 verdict would only be more forgiving.
